item.title: Trump meets Putin envoy, says Ukraine peace deal could come very soon
item.description: Trump said he had met Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev privately and predicted a Ukraine deal could emerge soon, as US officials discussed security guarantees with Kyiv and European partners.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said he met privately on Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin's envoy after the Russian official appeared alongside representatives from Ukraine at a White House event organised by US First Lady Melania Trump. Trump would not disclose what he discussed with Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev but predicted a deal could emerge soon aimed at resolving the Russian war in Ukraine. A US delegation is scheduled to mediate talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 between representatives from Russia and Ukraine. Trump, speaking to reporters at the White House, said the war was close to being settled and that ending it might involve all of Europe. “It's going to be a big agreement, and it's going to involve more than Ukraine ... I could even say it might involve all of Europe. It's going to be a big, beautiful agreement, and everyone's going to be thrilled,” Trump said. Trump has frequently predicted that an agreement to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War Two was close. However, negotiations have picked up in recent weeks. Trump said he did not meet the Ukrainian delegation on Thursday. Trump envoy Jared Kushner said US officials meeting in Brussels on Thursday held “productive and substantive discussions” with Ukraine, NATO and European partners on security guarantees for Ukraine and a broader European security architecture. Kushner said in a social media post that negotiators were exploring five principal goals: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability. “Any arrangements must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independent decision-making of every nation,” Kushner said. “Each country will retain authority over its own security and alliances, and no country would have a veto over another's sovereign choices. “NATO will remain central to European collective defence, and this initiative would build upon existing institutions and commitments.” FIRST LADY BRINGS TWO SIDES TOGETHER Dmitriev was among the officials at the rare face-to-face event with Ukrainian representatives at the White House to mark a six-day ceasefire that Melania Trump helped broker in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky. The deal expired on Sunday. “We have chosen humanity over war,” the First Lady said at the event. “We must use the courage we brought to Oleshky to find common ground through a shared concern for the suffering of innocent people.” Melania Trump said she was “involved in every stage of the planning” of the temporary ceasefire, including reviewing aerial images and assessing roadways and hospital access. President Trump, who did not attend the event, has lauded his wife's role in the Oleshky ceasefire, telling reporters in October that “she does better than our professionals”. Ukrainian lawmaker David Arakhamia and Dmytro Lubinets, the country's human rights ombudsman, also attended the event. They urged Slovenian-born Melania Trump to continue her peace efforts. Both sides presented the First Lady with thank-you gifts. Russia's Dmitriev gave her a drawing of pink hearts from a girl from Oleshky and said the child “chose to live with her family in Russia”, referring to the dispute over displaced Ukrainian children in Russia. “I love Melania,” the drawing read. The Ukrainians presented the First Lady with a state award “for your brave heart, for saving our people, and for returning back Ukrainian children”. She handed the visiting delegations letters addressed to Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. DEMOCRATS TAKE MAJORITY IN CONGRESS The visit marked the first in-person contact between Russian and US officials since Tuesday's midterm elections, when Democrats ousted Republicans from control of Congress in a blow to Trump. The Democratic majority in Congress, starting in January, is widely expected to push for more aid for Ukraine and question the Republican president's decisions to strike a diesel deal with Russia and ease some sanctions on Moscow. Trump has increased his criticism of Zelenskiy in recent weeks. The Kremlin has said it hopes Trump will continue his peacemaking efforts despite the Republican Party's defeat. It has also said preparations were under way for a meeting between Putin, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China's southern city of Shenzhen this month. Dmitriev previously met Trump's special envoy, Steve Witkoff, at the White House in 2025. Trump's predecessor, Joe Biden, did not invite any Russian officials to the White House. Dmitriev has been involved in facilitating the release of American detainees in Russia, the reunification of Ukrainian children with their families, and the humanitarian operation in Oleshky.

item.title: Street remains bullish on Titan Company post Q2, stronger Q3 prospects
item.description: Analysts remain positive on Titan after its Q2 earnings, citing resilient jewellery demand, improving watch and eyewear performance, and stronger festive prospects in Q3 ...
item.dc:creator: Devangshu Datta
item.content:encoded: Tata group jewellery-to-watches retailer Titan Company’s consolidated revenue from operations grew 10 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to ₹20,610 crore in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27); excluding bullion, growth would be 23 per cent. Standalone jewellery revenue (ex-bullion) rose 22 per cent Y-o-Y, though demand was impacted by the festive season’s shift from Q2 in FY26 to Q3 in FY27. (This will also impact Q3FY27 comparisons). Volatile gold prices also impacted sales. Footfalls improved at the end of October 2026. Q3FY27 may see growth with a boost from festive buying. Stable gold prices may improve margins and volumes.

item.title: Sebi warns Dabur India over delay in disclosing USFDA warning letter
item.description: The market regulator has cautioned Dabur India over delayed disclosure of a USFDA warning letter, saying repeated violations could attract enforcement action under Sebi rules.
item.dc:creator: Sharleen Dsouza
item.content:encoded: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Friday issued a warning to Dabur India for delaying the disclosure of a warning letter issued by the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) in July, the company said in a stock exchange filing. In its letter, the market regulator noted that the non-compliance was viewed seriously and advised the company’s board to be careful in the future to avoid lapses. “Any repetition of such violation in future will be viewed seriously and appropriate enforcement action would be initiated in accordance with the provisions of the SEBI Act, 1992, the Rules, the Regulations or Circulars issued thereunder,” said the letter, which the company uploaded on the exchanges. The letter added that the communication from Sebi should be placed before the board of directors at the upcoming board meeting and its comments should be forwarded to the regulator. Dabur India said that the warning letter issued by Sebi had no impact on the company's financial operations and other activities.

item.title: SP Group's Eqyizen plans to raise up to $200 mn via rupee bonds: Bankers
item.description: The Shapoorji Pallonji Group unit plans to issue zero-coupon rupee-denominated bonds maturing in July 2029, with the fundraising expected to be completed by the end of November, bankers said ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / News / SP Group's Eqyizen plans to raise up to $200 mn via rupee bonds: Bankers

SP Group's Eqyizen plans to raise up to $200 mn via rupee bonds: Bankers The Shapoorji Pallonji Group unit plans to issue zero-coupon rupee-denominated bonds maturing in July 2029, with the fundraising expected to be completed by the end of November, bankers said

Bankers said some of the company's approved borrowing limit remains unutilised and it wants to reach its fundraising target | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 06 2026 | 3:58 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's Eqyizen Investment, a unit of Shapoorji Pallonji Group, plans to raise around $150 million to $200 million of rupee equivalent funds through the sale of zero-coupon rupee-denominated bonds maturing in July 2029, two bankers said on Friday. "The company will finalise the quantum that it intends to borrow in rupee terms and should be done with the issuance before end of November," one of the bankers mentioned above said. The bankers spoke on the condition of anonymity, while the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. Bankers said some of the company's approved borrowing limit remains unutilised and it wants to reach its fundraising target.   In October, Eqyizen Investment had raised around ₹4,450 crore (about $473 million) through a similar debt issuance at a yield of 18.95%, after raising around ₹21,350 crore via another issue at the same yield in July. In both these instances, Mercury Finance, another SP Group firm, had raised funds through zero-coupon US dollar-denominated bonds due July 2029 and invested the proceeds in rupee securities of Eqyizen. The outlook for the real estate conglomerate's bonds has improved after Tata Trusts, Tata Sons' controlling shareholder, said that SP Group had proposed a plan to sell ₹25,000 crore worth of its stake in Tata Sons. The proposal has yet to move forward amid differences between Tata Trusts and Tata Sons.
